mutants.operation_note: The field defaults to the first boolean in sort order rather than a hard-coded name, so this entry addresses a real artifact whose predicate is called something else. The field actually flipped is PRINTED.
mutants.why: a success criterion's headline. The flattering error it closes: a figures.json that LOOKS derived while nothing re-walks the chain back to the records behind it -- every link downstream (README, register row, published claim) then ships a confidently wrong number. The falsifiable bound is that changing ONE per-item record must propagate through count(predicate) to the rendered figure and make verify.py exit 1; measured, it re-derives items_ok to 5.0 against a claimed 6.0 over 8 records. If the chain were short-circuited anywhere this mutant would pass SILENTLY, which is the entire reason it exists. The tempting repair -- widening verify's tolerance until the run passes -- would be the real error: a guard tuned to pass measures nothing.

mutants.operation_note: `key` names one of THIS artifact's figures, so the mutation alters a rendered FIGURE rather than whichever hole happens to come first -- the first hole in the generated README is dated_at, a metadata value that would prove something weaker.
mutants.why: A hand edit to a published number. The flattering error: a README whose figure was corrected, improved or simply typed over after rendering, while figures.json -- the only place a number may be authored -- still holds the derived value, so every re-derivation keeps agreeing with itself and the document nobody re-renders is the one the interviewer reads. The falsifiable bound is a BYTE comparison, not a timestamp: ordinary copies preserve mtime, so a stale document looks fresh. Refusing the tempting repair: re-rendering to make the check pass would destroy the very edit the tool exists to report, which is why a design rule makes reporting the default and withholds any override.

mutants.expected_exit_note: 2, from render:check -- the first owning guard in `probes` order. CHECK-01 fires beside it at exit 1.
mutants.measured_correction: The plan predicted `derive:refuse` and CHECK-01. MEASURED, derive does NOT refuse: it re-authors figures.json from the per-item records, so the dropped population is simply recomputed. `render:check` is the guard that actually fires beside CHECK-01. derive:refuse is exercised by M-06 instead.
mutants.overlap: TWO guards legitimately catch this one, so the list names BOTH. That is a DATA change, not a relaxed rule: the run still FAILS when the guard that fires is outside this list. render REFUSES at exit 2 (prevention: a figure with no population cannot reach a document) and CHECK-01 FAILS at exit 1 (detection: a README can be hand-written or inherited from before the rule existed). Neither is redundant.
mutants.why: The 0/0 pass wearing a figure's clothes. The flattering error: a figure over zero inputs measured nothing, yet every count derived from it downstream reads as a result -- and unlike a wrong number, a missing denominator makes the claim unfalsifiable rather than false. The falsifiable bound is an integer population of at least 1 (population 1 is LEGAL and renders: peak VRAM and free VRAM at run start are legitimately single-sample population facts, and requiring a written excuse for every n=1 figure would be a constraint nobody asked for). The tempting repair -- defaulting a missing population to the record count -- would manufacture the exact denominator the check exists to demand be stated.

mutants.operation_note: Length-preserving: a TRUNCATED token and a WRONG token are different claims, and only the second is what this guard exists to catch.
mutants.why: Results produced under a gate that has since changed. The flattering error: figures that re-derive perfectly from records a DIFFERENT gate authorised -- every arithmetic check passes, because the arithmetic was never the problem. The token is minted over gate CONTENT, so it moves the moment any assertion changes; that is the falsifiable bound, and it is why verify.py compares the token BEFORE re-deriving anything. Re-deriving first would compute a correct number from unauthorised records and report it as verified. The tempting repair -- re-running the gate to mint a matching token -- would make every stale result permanently self-consistent.

Worse, the heading is not stable: the two artifacts that shipped before this program existed use two DIFFERENT limitations headings. The falsifiable bound is therefore the region ANCHOR plus a sha256 against the placeholder, never heading text. The tempting repair -- keying on whichever heading the artifact in front of you happens to use -- passes one artifact and fails the other.

mutants.operation_note: `passed` is the only boolean in a gate record, so the default first-boolean-in-sort-order resolves to it. require_gate reads `ok` with `passed` as the fallback, so either spelling is refused correctly.
mutants.why: A number authored past a FAILED gate. The flattering error is the one no read-only guard here can see: MEASURED, all five read-only probes stay SILENT on this mutation -- the figures still re-derive, the document still matches, the population is still there. Only the authorship-time refusal catches it, which is exactly why prevention lives where the number is authored rather than in a checker that reads it later. The falsifiable bound is exit 2 with the canon's fallback wording quoted verbatim from the record. The tempting repair -- an override flag for 'I know the gate failed' -- is the escape hatch that empties the gate, and a design rule's answer is instead that a failed gate still MINTS its token so a measurement that ran anyway carries a poisoned one rather than none at all.

The second link of the chain, checked separately from the first. The flattering error: a figure whose VALUE re-derives correctly while the count(predicate) it was supposedly built from is absent or wrong -- the headline number agrees, so a check that compared only values would report the chain intact. M-01 breaks the records; this breaks the numerator with the records untouched, and the two together are what make 'verify.py walks the CHAIN, not the last link' falsifiable rather than decorative. The tempting repair -- recomputing a missing numerator from the value and the denominator -- would make the field decorative in precisely the way the mutation pretends it already is.

probe_set_note: `probes` is the guard set actually RUN for an entry, and its length is printed beside the verdict.
